key_insight: Localizing medical evaluation rubrics for Japan reveals item-level scoring errors that stable model rankings can conceal.
clinical_relevance: Japan-specific rubrics can better credit responses aligned with local healthcare institutions, medications, and care pathways.
method: Adapted HealthBench into 79 Japanese patient-facing consultations with 1,022 evaluation criteria.
Used source-cited LLM drafting, specialist revision, independent dual-physician review, and meta-review.
Compared localized and machine-translated rubrics across 18 LLMs.
evidence_signal: Rankings remained broadly consistent (τ=0.817), but verdicts flipped on 17.7% of modified criteria versus 7.3% re-grading noise; localization reduced false penalties on Japan-adapted negative criteria by 7.1 percentage points.
watch_item: Results cover 79 consultations and benchmark scoring, not demonstrated improvements in patient outcomes or real-world clinical safety.
paper_title: JHealthBench-L: Clinician-Reviewed Localization of HealthBench for Rubric-Based Medical LLM Evaluation in Japan
